 NAPLES, Fla. - It's been quite a year for Joshua Grant. 
 An unexpected phone call sent the 19-year-old FC Naples goalkeeper rushing to the airport for another opportunity to represent his country. 
 Grant received his third call-up to Jamaica's senior national team after starting goalkeeper Andre Blake suffered an injury ahead of the team's matchup against Mexico. 
 "I really wasn't expecting it," Grant told WINK News in an exclusive Zoom interview. "I get a call. 'Josh, we need you in Jamaica tomorrow.'" 
 Grant immediately packed his bags and caught a flight out of Miami that same night. 
 "I ran, told my mom. She was ecstatic, so it was definitely amazing," he said. 
 Grant joined Jamaica ahead of two matches against Mexico, beginning Saturday, Nov. 14, in Kingston, followed by a rematch Tuesday in Monterrey, Mexico. 
 Despite being just 19 years old, Grant is no stranger to representing his country. 
 He first joined Jamaica's youth national team at 15 and became the first Jamaican goalkeeper to compete in two CONCACAF Under-20 Championships. 
 Now, after signing his first professional contract with FC Naples earlier this year, Grant believes he's earned his place among Jamaica's top talent. 
 "Having that skill, having that level of talent that God has given me is like, it's inevitable for me to be here," Grant said. "I've put everything into this. This is my life. So for me to be here is like, yeah, Josh, I've earned it and I feel good about it." 
 And while Grant is focused on his international opportunity, he also revealed some big news for FC Naples fans. 
 "FC Naples has exercised my option. So I'll be staying at FC Naples for another year and I'm excited," Grant said. 
 The announcement means the fan favorite will return to Southwest Florida for another season in 2027. 
 "I'm looking forward to playing a lot of games, getting a lot of professional minutes under my belt," Grant said. 
 For now, though, Grant's focus is on Jamaica's national team, where he's hoping to make the most of his latest opportunity. 
 "Something on my list is to make my debut, so looking forward to that soon," he said. 
 But representing Jamaica carries a meaning that extends well beyond soccer. 
 "Every time I put these colors on, I think about my grandmother. Think about my mom who fought to get to America and to give me a better life," Grant said. "This is my grandmother, my mother born on this soil," Grant said. "So it's a different type of feeling and a different type of grit that I try and play with just because of that factor."
